intro: A Seattle songwriter with a two-decade catalog.
story: Damien Jurado is a Seattle songwriter who made The Horizon Just Laughed, his first self-produced album, for Secretly Canadian in 2018. He played Pickathon in 2019, the year In the Shape of a Storm came out on Mama Bird, recorded in two hours on one California afternoon. The Monster Who Hated Pennsylvania followed in 2021 on his own Maraqopa label, and Did Something In Me Break in 2026.
artist_reel_line: The Monster Who Hated Pennsylvania came in 2021; Did Something In Me Break in 2026.

intro: A Halifax band led by the songwriter Nigel Chapman.
story: Nap Eyes is a Halifax band led by the songwriter Nigel Chapman, a scientist by day. Thought Rock Fish Scale, recorded live with no overdubs, made the Polaris longlist in 2016, and I'm Bad Now came out in 2018. They played Pickathon in 2019. Snapshot of a Beginner followed in 2020 and The Neon Gate in 2024, and in 2025 they toured the U.S. with MJ Lenderman.
artist_reel_line: Snapshot of a Beginner in 2020, The Neon Gate in 2024.

story: Makaya McCraven is a Chicago drummer and producer whose 2015 debut, In the Moment, was cut from a year of recorded live shows. Universal Beings, a double album recorded live and in studios across Chicago, New York, Los Angeles and London, came out on International Anthem in 2018 and put his edited-live method on the map. He played Pickathon in 2019. In These Times followed in 2022, and in 2025 he released four EPs, collected as the double LP Off the Record.
artist_reel_line: In These Times came in 2022; in 2025, four EPs collected as Off the Record.
